references.text: Moses shepherds the flock of his father-in-law Jethro, who is also called Reuel, the priest of Midian
Zipporah, Moses' wife, circumcises their son
Jethro brings Zipporah and Moses' two sons back to him after he had sent her away
Hobab, son of Reuel the Midianite, is mentioned as Moses' father-in-law
Miriam and Aaron speak against Moses because of the Cushite woman he had married
Abraham's servant is tasked with finding a wife for Isaac, a pattern of marriage arranged by a father
Laban gives his daughters Leah and Rachel to Jacob as wives, a similar pattern where a father gives his daughter in marriage
The Kenites, descendants of Moses' father-in-law, are mentioned in connection with Judah
Heber the Kenite had separated from the Kenites, descendants of Hobab, Moses' father-in-law
Stephen's speech mentions that Moses fled and became a foreigner in the land of Midian, where he had two sons
The reference links the marriage in Midian with later reunion and Jethro's role.
Complementary verses defining the start and end points of Moses' stay with his father-in-law.
